title: Temporal RBAC Zones with SCIM Delta Snapshots and Certification Export
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a mechanism to create timeboxed RBAC 'zones' (logical access slices) and produce tamper-evident SCIM delta snapshots for periodic certification exports. This ticket covers the runtime access model, SCIM snapshot format, export orchestration, and a lightweight proof bundle that maps identities, roles, session metadata (SSO), and the retention policy applied at snapshot creation. The feature should enable auditors to verify who had access during a specific window and show automated evidence linking SCIM deltas + SSO session exports to retention/ residency controls.
background: Current periodic review process is manual: we export full user lists and role mappings, then reconcile in spreadsheets. That creates sprawl, takes days, and makes it hard to prove historical role state for a given date range. We need a reproducible artifact that captures deltas and contextual SSO signals (session start/ end, session IP, SAML assertion ID) to reduce reviewer effort and provide deterministic evidence for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Create RBAC zone primitives (zone id, start_ts, end_ts, allowed-roles list) and an API to materialize a zone for a tenant.
Produce SCIM delta snapshots for a zone: additions, removals, role changes with ISO8601 timestamps and actor (service/automation/user).
Include correlated SSO session exports covering the zone time window: session id, user id, start/end, auth-method, assertion-id.

Generate a zipped certification export bundle (SCIM-delta.json, sso-sessions.json, manifest.txt, signed-hash.txt) via a background job and store in tenant's audit bucket for N days per retention policy.
Expose a Console view and API endpoint to request and download certification bundles; requests must be rate-limited and audited.
End-to-end tests that validate bundle contents and verify signed-hash matches bundle payload for tamper evidence.
Documentation in Confluence describing data fields, privacy considerations, and operator runbook for requesting manual replays.
Security review completed and KMS signing key rotation documented for export signing.
Performance: generating a bundle for a tenant with 200k users and 1M session records must complete within 30 minutes when run on dedicated export worker fleet.
implementation_notes: Introduce zone table: (zone_id, tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, created_by, status).
SCIM delta generator will stream from user-change CDC topic and materialize a minimal JSON containing {op, user_id, roles, ts, actor}.
SSO session collector: extend current session export job to accept time window and include SAML/OIDC assertion metadata where available.
Signing: use KMS asymmetric key to sign a SHA256 digest of the sorted bundle files; store signature alongside bundle manifest.
Retention: integrate with retention service to apply tenant's retention setting to certification bundles; allow 'export-ttl' override for legal hold.
UI: Console -> Security -> Access Certification -> Request export. Show progress, estimated size, and secure link expiration policy.
RBAC enforcement: only accounts with 'audit:export' permission can request or download bundles; add audit events for request/download actions.
Backfill: provide a controlled backfill path to generate historical zones for legal requests; requires operator approval and adds to cost metrics.
Telemetry: track export size, generation time, failure reasons, and requestor identity for SLA reporting.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large tenants produce very large bundles causing timeouts. Mitigation: chunked streaming export and resumable bundle writer; estimate size before generation.
Risk: Sensitive PII in session logs. Mitigation: PII redaction rules, configurable field masks per tenant; document redaction behaviour in export manifest.
Risk: Unauthorized export requests. Mitigation: require two-step approval for exports older than 1 year or >X GB; use 'audit:export' role gate and email notification to tenant admins.
Risk: Signature key compromise. Mitigation: KMS rotation, short-lived signing keys, and a signature revocation list accessible to auditors.
Risk: Compliance/regulatory differences per region. Mitigation: apply residency-aware export routing so bundles for EU tenants remain in EU storage and are exported from EU workers.
